title: Balanced derived scalar tensor and regular coefficient arrow
statement: Use the exact scalar restriction $s$ for an arbitrary condensed ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$ from [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants], and the ordinary and derived internal tensors and trivial coefficient objects of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup]. Define the ordinary lax scalar tensor comparison $sM\otimes_RsN\to s(M\otimes_{R'}N)$ as the unique balanced comparison taking every generalized pure tensor to that same pure tensor over $R'$, and its unit to be $\varphi:R\to sR'$. The comparison on total complexes is the unique chain map whose restriction to each degree summand is that ordinary comparison. The lax structure on $D(s)$ is uniquely fixed by its computation equation with the canonical tensor localization maps, termwise scalar-restriction localization factors, and the total-complex comparison, together with the corresponding unit equation. This uses K-flat $R'$-representatives and never assumes their scalar restrictions are $R$-flat. Let the regular scalar module map be the unique internal linear map with underlying condensed additive map $\varphi$. Regard it as an equivariant map of trivial actions using the normalized underlying scalar comparison, and then as the actual degree-zero derived coefficient arrow. The map $C_R(J)\to sC_{R'}(J)$ is $c_J$ applied to this arrow.
